title: Circuit breaker weekly brief — May 28 2027
body:
Summary:
This week the primary narrative for SRE was a repeatable circuit-breaker cascade that surfaced when a new client retry configuration (deployed 2027-05-20) interacted poorly with request throttling during a regional capacity squeeze. Incident windows were short (sub-30m) but produced a measurable SLO blip for token-generation latency on the eu-west-1 region.

Key outcomes:
- Root cause: client-side aggressive retry + our in-region circuit-breaker thresholds were conservative, causing cascaded rejections and temporary hotspotting on a subset of worker pods.
- User impact: elevated p99 token latency for 18 minutes on 2027-05-25 15:12–15:30 UTC in eu-west-1; error rate remained within SRE alerting thresholds but latency SLO (p99 < 350ms) was breached for the window.
- Mitigation: temporary relax of circuit-breaker tripping threshold + transient autoscale policy increased worker pool by 12% for the region; client team rolled back retry change as a short-term safety measure.

Incidents (concise timeline):
1) 2027-05-25 15:08 UTC — First alert from latency-watchdog: p99 token gen exceeded 350ms for 2 consecutive intervals. Pager ops engaged.
2) 15:12 — Error-budget-monitor flagged a small rolling SLO breach; on-call rotated to bridge room.
3) 15:14 — Observability shows increased reject_count from circuit-breaker on 3/10 pods; request fan-out from upstream retries observed.
4) 15:18 — Applied hotfix: increase breaker tripping threshold by 20% (config push d/sre/cb/relax-20270525).
5) 15:22 — Autoscale policy triggered a transient scale-up; worker latencies trended down.
6) 15:30 — SLO returned to normal; post incident monitoring kept expanded pool for 30 minutes.

Technical analysis (short):
- What happened: a client SDK change (PR ref SRE-482) changed retry from exponential backoff with jitter to a faster capped-linear retry. Under normal load that's fine, but during a tight capacity window the increased retry density created microbursts on the same hot key shards. Our circuit-breaker counter (rolling window of 30s with tripping at 40% rejects) started tripping pods; client repeated retries amplified the effect and caused traffic redistribution that produced transient higher queueing on a subset of pods.
- Why the breaker tripped: thresholds tuned for steady-state overload mitigation, not for coordinated client retry patterns. The behavioral coupling between client retry logic and our breaker state machine produced the cascade.
- Metrics to inspect: reject_count, breaker_open_time, queue_length, p99_token_latency, cpu_utilization per pod, request_src counts by client-id.

SLO snapshot (eu-west-1, week ending 2027-05-28):
- p99 token latency: 0.36s (SLO: 0.35s) — small miss driven by the one window above
- availability (5xx rate): 99.98% (target 99.9%) — within target
- error budget remaining: 99.2% (no escalation required)
- Notes: global aggregates unaffected; incident localized to eu-west-1 and short-lived.

On-call handoff (to next shift):
- Active items: monitor SRE-482 rollback verification + confirm client-side SDK rollback (owner: Ethan Park).
- Triage checklist: watch breaker_open_time, p99_token_latency; alert if p99 > 400ms for 3 intervals OR breaker_opened_pods > 4 for > 2 consecutive intervals.
- Who to call: client-team slack (#client-sdk), infra-autoscale (pager rule), MCC (for capacity emergencies).
- Known mitigations in place: breaker config temporary relax applied; autoscale policy has 30% burst headroom for next 2 hours.

Runbook and process gaps discovered:
- Breaker tuning not documented for coordinated client-induced microbursts. Runbook only covered steady overload scenarios.
- Missing observability slice: request-source breakdown by retry-attempt index (we can’t easily see attempt-level fan-out in dashboards).
- Rollback coordination: SDK rollback lacked a direct rollback playbook and required manual coordination via pm.

Immediate action items (owner / ETA):
- Add an 'attempt_index' tag to request logs and augment dashboards (owner: Priya Nambiar / ETA: 2027-06-03).
- Create a runbook section for "client retry interactions" with recommended breaker thresholds and emergency mitigations (owner: Maya Chen / ETA: 2027-06-01).
- Post-mortem doc + RCA draft (link will be SRE-482 postmortem) (owner: Ethan Park / ETA: 2027-05-31).
- Implement automated rollback verifier for client SDK changes that increased retries (infra git action) (owner: Luis Martinez / ETA: 2027-06-07).

Longer-term proposals (backlog):
- Adaptive breaker thresholds that temporarily widen the tripping window on detecting high retry density from a single client-id. Modeling underway in design doc: Confluence link above.
- Client-facing SDK policy: if a client increases retry density, require a staged rollout with traffic shaping flags. Work item to coordinate with product.
- Improve chaos testing to simulate coordinated client retries against a partial region to validate breaker behavior.

Meetings / syncs this week (notes):
- Incident retro (2027-05-26): quick 45m sync; attendees: SRE+Client SDK+Infra. Actioned immediate rollback and runbook owners.
- Latency sync (2027-05-27): discussed need for attempt-level visibility and sampling strategy to avoid log explosion. Decided to sample 1% of requests with full attempt tracing.

Miscellaneous operational notes / FYIs:
- We observed a smaller unrelated pod eviction event in us-west-2 on 2027-05-24 (caused by noisy neighbor on shared gpu node). Separate ticket created: INFRA-621. No overlap with the circuit-breaker event.
- Cost impact of temporary scale-up this week estimated at +0.6% for eu-west-1 (negligible vs reliability benefit).

Handoff log (end-of-shift):
- Last checked: 2027-05-28 17:45 UTC by Maya Chen.
- Environment state: breaker relaxed, autoscale burst enabled, SDK rollback confirmed on canary traffic (10%) and pending full rollback.
- Next on-call: Luis Martinez (primary) at 2027-05-28 18:00 UTC. Luis to watch the three lead metrics for 2 hours and confirm system stability.

Appendix (quick links / dashboards):
- Latency dashboard (eu-west-1): /dashboards/latency/eu-west-1
- Circuit-breaker telemetry: /dashboards/sre/circuit-breaker
- Request tracing sampler config: /infra/tracing/sampler-configs

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally concise; a full post-mortem with timeline, logs, and annotated graphs will be attached to SRE-482. Please add any missed items as comments and assign runbook tasks if you take them on.

End of brief.
